messages:
Aisha Patel: Morning team — quick sprint. Drafted a compact battlecard for the webinar + SDR handoff. I pasted the lead soundbites below, need micro edits by 11:30 PT. :rocket:
Aisha Patel: Draft link: <https://docs.google.com/draft-battlecard|battlecard-draft> (please comment inline)
Tom Liu: scanning now. will flag any legaly risky claims but quick thought — push the cost/lambda comparison higher up. buyers care faster than tech detail.
Priya Singh: Agreed. Also add a short line about fallbacks: "predictable SLAs + graceful downgrade to cheaper variants" — makes it tangible.
Noah Carter: Can we avoid absolute numbers w/o context? bench-bot had different runs last week. Add a caveat like "typical 95p latency on common prompts" rather than a single claim.
Caroline Vega: Proposed one-liners for top of card: 
- "Production inference, not research experiments — predictable latency and unit cost."
- "Same API for hosted, reserved, and on-prem: ship once, route anywhere."
Pick one and I can craft the microcopy.
Aisha Patel: Love those. Pick second one for webinar hero. Caroline, can you make 8–10 options for A/B testing in the slide deck?
Caroline Vega: On it. Will drop options in the slide deck and mark variant A/B.
benchmark-bot: nightly-bench: 2025-03-18 06:12Z | sample-workload (chat-like): hosted-rc1 95p=128ms, cloudX-managed 95p=210ms, infraY 95p=190ms. All runs use 2k prompt median. See attached CSV.
Noah Carter: Thanks bench-bot. Adding note: include hardware parity footnote (GPU types) in appendix. avoids pushback.
Tom Liu: For SDRs — can we have 3 TL;DR rebut lines vs cloud vendors: 1) routing + fallbacks, 2) predictable unit economics, 3) first-class private deploys. Short and skimmable.
Priya Singh: I'll write those as quick scripts. Also add procurement objection: "we can provide usage elasticity without long infra rebuilds" — helps infra teams.
Aisha Patel: Action items: Caroline — hero copy + A/B options (due 10:30 PT). Priya — SDR rebut scripts (due 11:00 PT). Tom — legal check + procurement line signoff (11:15 PT). Noah — appendix bench note + hardware footnote (11:30 PT).
Tom Liu: noted. tagging @legal later if needed.
Priya Singh: Putting scripts in #marketing-playbooks channel when done.
Caroline Vega: uploaded 10 variants to the deck: <https://slides.app/deck-ops|deck link>. Marked favs in comments.
Aisha Patel: Perfect. Final ask — avoid the word "cheaper" alone; prefer "lower unit cost" or "cost-efficient". Small edit but protects claims.
Noah Carter: +1 on phrasing. Also suggest one-sentence benchmark callout: "Under representative customer workloads, Redwood Inference shows ~40–45% lower per-token cost at comparable latency vs cloud-managed offerings (see appendix for test conditions)." (Priya/Tom, ok to use ~40%?)
Tom Liu: I'll vet the percentage with legal/benching. If bench confirms, we can phrase as "~40%" with appendix link.
Aisha Patel: Great — thanks all. Will assemble final battlecard and ping go/no-go at 11:40 PT. :white_check_mark:
